WPT|/ca.tech.sub: What happens inside a concrete that carries the crystalline admixture from the day it is poured: where the active ingredient sits, what wakes it, how the pores close throughout the depth of the component — and why a crack years later closes itself. Schematic, at the scale of the capillary pores; not to scale.
WPT|/ca.tech.player: Micro scale · inside the hardened cement paste, step by step
WPT|/ca.tech.aria: 3D animation of the crystalline reaction inside a concrete made with the admixture
WPT|/ca.tech.hint: Drag to look round · the offset stays until replay
WPT|/ca.tech.steps/0/0: In the mix from day one
WPT|/ca.tech.steps/0/1: The admixture is dosed into the fresh concrete — 1.75–2.25 % of the cement weight for the liquids {CL170} and {CL210}, 0.75–1.25 % for the powders {CP360} and {CP350} — and distributed through the whole volume by the mixer. When the cement hydrates the active ingredient is locked into the hardened cement paste: in every pore wall, at every depth, not only on a surface.
WPT|/ca.tech.steps/1/1: Hardened cement paste is porous: capillary pores of roughly 0.01 to 10 µm link up into a network. Under ground water or a filled tank this network draws water in by capillary suction and pressure. In a plain concrete that water runs on to the reinforcement and through separating cracks into the building.
WPT|/ca.tech.steps/2/0: The active ingredient dissolves and reacts
WPT|/ca.tech.steps/2/1: The pore water dissolves the active ingredient where it meets it. Deep in the pores it reacts with what every cement hydration leaves behind — calcium hydroxide (portlandite, Ca(OH)₂) — and with the dissolved CO₂: insoluble crystalline phases form. The concrete supplies the second reactant; the crystals are part of the concrete, not a foreign material in it.
WPT|/ca.tech.steps/3/1: Needle-shaped crystals grow from the pore walls into the pore space and interlock. Because the active ingredient is everywhere, growth starts wherever water arrives — at the ground side, along a crack, around an aggregate grain — not from one surface inwards. The micrographs show the acicular clusters packing the capillary pore structure.
WPT|/ca.tech.steps/4/0: The capillaries are blocked — the zone shifts outwards
WPT|/ca.tech.steps/4/1: Where the crystals have grown, the pore is too narrow for liquid water. The capillary zone of the component, the depth to which water is drawn in, moves outwards; ground moisture and pressurised water are conducted much less far into the concrete and stay away from the reinforcement. Water vapour still diffuses: the concrete dries instead of trapping moisture behind a film.
WPT|/ca.tech.steps/5/1: Concrete cracks — shrinkage, settlement, temperature. A surface or continuous crack up to 0.4 mm (tapering down to 0.5 mm) brings water in, and with it the reaction restarts: unreacted active ingredient at the crack faces dissolves and fresh crystals bridge the gap. Crack injections for non-dynamic separating cracks up to 0.4 mm can often be omitted. Movements can reopen a sealed crack — then it heals again.
WPT|/ca.tech.steps/6/1: Less water means less of what the water carries: chloride ion migration is reduced and the carbonation rate is lower ({CL210}, {CP360}), the frost and freeze–thaw resistance improves. The reinforcement stays in the dry core. By the BAW method — service life from the chloride migration coefficient — a test report shows a 2.5-fold service life against the reference concrete.
WPT|/ca.tech.steps/7/0: Permanently active, for the life of the component
WPT|/ca.tech.steps/7/1: Not all of the active ingredient is consumed. What remains lies dormant in the matrix and waits for water — for decades. No film to age, no seam to fail, nothing to renew: the waterproofing is as durable as the concrete itself, and the sealant in {CL210} and {CP360} has been keeping the water absorption low from the first day.

WPT|/ca.tech.caps/5: A later crack fills with crystals and closes

WPT|/ca.tech.rxn.title: The two effects, in two lines
WPT|/ca.tech.rxn.hyd: The crystalline effect of all four products — the active ingredient in the hardened paste meets water and the lime of the hydration:
WPT|/ca.tech.rxn.hydEq: active ingredient + Ca(OH)₂ + H₂O (+ CO₂) → insoluble crystalline calcium silicate hydrate / CaCO₃ in the pores and cracks
WPT|/ca.tech.rxn.ic: The second effect of the 2-in-1 products — a sealant after DIN EN 934-2 integrated in {CL210} and {CP360}, a plasticiser in {CL170}:
WPT|/ca.tech.rxn.icEq: hydrophobic pore walls from the first day: capillary water absorption reduced by > 50 % immediately · {CL170}: water saving up to 10 %, lower w/c, smoother consistency
WPT|/ca.tech.rxn.note: Simplified. The composition of the active ingredients is proprietary; the mechanism is that of crystalline waterproofing technology and shows in the micrographs of the needle-shaped crystals in the capillary pore structure and in the tests of the data sheets and test reports: depth of water penetration under pressure (EN 12390-8), crack healing, chloride migration, freeze–thaw–salt, carbonation.
WPT|/ca.tech.needs.title: What the technology needs — and what it does not do
WPT|/ca.tech.needs/0/1: Cement ≥ 270 kg/m³ (CEM I), ≥ 290 (CEM II), ≥ 380 (CEM III/A); w/c < 0.55; fly ash ≤ 80 and granulated slag ≤ 100 kg/m³ added to the binder; grain size 16 mm (exceptionally 32 mm); component thickness ≥ 15 cm. CEM III/C is prohibited, CEM III/B for the liquids and {CP350}; lignite fly ash is of limited suitability. Preliminary tests are always necessary.
WPT|/ca.tech.needs/1/0: Water, to work and to keep working
WPT|/ca.tech.needs/1/1: The reaction runs in water: where no water arrives the active ingredient simply waits. That is the point — it reacts exactly where the concrete is loaded.
WPT|/ca.tech.needs/2/1: The admixture does not replace compaction, curing and the crack-width design: the planner and structural engineer set the crack-width limits, the concrete is produced, placed and post-treated to the valid standards. In rare cases the admixture influences the setting — {RUX} controls it.
WPT|/ca.tech.needs/3/1: The construction joint is the classic weak point: {CJ5}, the crystalline metal waterstop, {CJ6}, the swelling tape, and {CJ1}, the injection hose, are the accessories of the system. Moving cracks and joints wider than 0.4 mm are not self-healed — they are injected.
WPT|/ca.tech.needs/4/1: The crystals make the concrete watertight; they do not make it acid-proof. Concretes of exposure class XA3 (DIN EN 206-1 / DIN 1045-2) are excluded. Where the concrete itself is attacked, a resistant coating armours it.

WPT|/ca.tech.fld.title: Where the technology pays
WPT|/ca.tech.fld.sub: The fields in which BETOCRETE concrete is used today as the economical waterproofing — and to extend the service life of the component.
WPT|/ca.tech.fld/0/0: Foundations, base slabs and basement walls
WPT|/ca.tech.fld/0/1: Watertight concrete without an external membrane: no protection boards, no weather window, no damage during backfill. The construction joints get the crystalline waterstop; cracks up to 0.4 mm heal themselves.
WPT|/ca.tech.fld/1/0: Collection and retaining basins, tanks and containers
WPT|/ca.tech.fld/1/1: Water on the inside, for good: the dosed concrete seals from the inside out and heals the fine cracks a filled tank always sees. {CL170}, {CP360} and {CP350} are tested for drinking water.
WPT|/ca.tech.fld/2/0: Swimming pools embedded in the ground
WPT|/ca.tech.fld/2/1: Ground water from outside, pool water from inside: the whole section is watertight, vapour permeable and free of a lining that could lift.
WPT|/ca.tech.fld/3/1: Chlorides from de-icing salt are the enemy of the reinforcement: reduced chloride ion migration and lower carbonation speed keep the steel passive; frost and freeze–thaw resistance improve.
WPT|/ca.tech.fld/4/0: Tunnels and concrete pipes, drains and manhole access points
WPT|/ca.tech.fld/4/1: Pre-cast or in-situ: the admixture goes into the mix at the plant, the component arrives watertight. Shotcrete is an application too.
WPT|/ca.tech.fld/5/0: Cooling towers and power stations, water and wastewater structures
WPT|/ca.tech.fld/5/1: Infrastructure that must not leak and cannot be renewed easily: one pour, one component, no renewal cycle. Exposure class XA3 is excluded; aggressive media need an armouring coating.
WPT|/ca.tech.fld/6/1: Soil and seepage water behind, frost and salt in front: the hydrophobic sealant of {CL210} and {CP360} lowers the water absorption at once, the crystals follow. {CL210} shows the highest effectiveness in exposure class XS.
WPT|/ca.tech.fld/7/1: The deepest point of the building, below the ground water, reachable only from the inside: cast watertight from the start, dry from the first day, no pump running for years.

WPT|/ca.lcc.title: In the mix once — or a renewal cycle
WPT|/ca.lcc.sub: Whole-life costing in the sense of ISO 15686-5: every cost that a waterproofing causes from the pour to the end of the planning horizon — application, protection layers, renewals with the access they need, upkeep. Set the model with your own rates: the defaults are relative planning values (installed cost of the BETOCRETE concrete’s waterproofing = 100 per m² of component), not quotations.

WPT|/ca.lcc.why.title: Why the curves separate
WPT|/ca.lcc.why/0/0: No separate trade, no protection layer
WPT|/ca.lcc.why/0/1: The waterproofing becomes an integral part of the component as early as the production of the concrete in the plant. Subsequent liquid waterproofing can be omitted and does not have to be organised, carried out and monitored on site.
WPT|/ca.lcc.why/1/1: The crystals are as durable as the concrete; there is no film to age, so nothing is re-applied. BETOCRETE waterproofing works for a component’s lifetime — renovation cycles can be eliminated.
WPT|/ca.lcc.why/2/1: Crack injections for non-dynamic separating cracks up to 0.4 mm can often be omitted due to the crack-healing ability of the concrete.
WPT|/ca.lcc.why/3/1: Water kept out of the pores means chloride and carbon dioxide kept away from the reinforcement: the service life of the component itself is extended — the largest item of any life-cycle account.
WPT|/ca.lcc.note: Model, not a quotation. Nominal costs are summed as they fall due; present values discount every year’s cost at the rate set (ISO 15686-5). Downtime, the risk of leaks and the extended service life of the structure are not priced in — they favour the integral system further. Replace the defaults by the rates of your project.
